method.method_draft: First describe the visible tree: organisms 1 and 2 meet at node A, node A connects to node B, and organism 3 branches off at node B. From the text, identify the target organisms as 1 and 3. Trace organism 1 inward: 1 → A → B. Trace organism 3 inward: 3 → B. The first shared node on these paths is B, so the most recent common ancestor is Organism B.

With only one natural way to solve the item, this is the genuinely distinct core method.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to determine that the required relationship is the most recent common ancestor specifically for organisms 1 and 3.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the definition of most recent common ancestor: for two taxa, trace each taxon’s branch backward into the tree and find the nearest shared internal node before the paths diverge further back in time.
